oil.summary: Brent briefly broke $90/bbl in Asian trade before settling at $88.36, still up 11% on the month, as the US-Iran conflict entered a ninth day of air strikes and the Strait of Hormuz remained functionally paralysed for tanker transit. A Malta-flagged products tanker was reported anchored in the Strait near Oman as vessel operators grew increasingly reluctant to attempt passage. WTI lagged slightly at $81.90, off 0.72% on the day, while RBOB gasoline cratered 6% intraday despite the national pump average reportedly topping $4/gallon. Heating oil's 25.7% monthly surge reflects the tightest distillate picture. Reports of Iran secretly shipping 70 million barrels to China before the blockade was reimposed add a sanctions-evasion dimension to the supply story. India's crude import bill reportedly rose 60% year-on-year in Q2.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz effectively blocked: tanker operators halting transits amid active US-Iran military exchanges
Brent touched $90 intraday on fresh escalation; heating oil up 25.7% on the month as distillate inventories tighten
Demand-side pressure building: India import bill +60% YoY, US pump prices back above $4/gal

gas.summary: A sharp divergence between US and European gas markets dominated the session. Henry Hub fell 2.3% to $2.844/MMBtu and is now down 9.6% on the month, reflecting insulation from Hormuz disruptions given US domestic supply buffers. TTF, by contrast, surged 2.1% to €58.59/MWh and is up nearly 40% over the past month, driven by two compounding shocks: LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz have reportedly ground to a halt over the past three days according to tanker-tracking data, and Ukraine struck Russia's last operational gas refinery. China's second consecutive monthly rise in LNG imports is simultaneously tightening Atlantic Basin cargoes that European buyers need as alternatives. News flow for US domestic gas fundamentals is thin today.
drivers: Hormuz LNG halt: tanker-tracking data shows zero Hormuz LNG exports for roughly three days, squeezing European spot supply
Ukraine struck Russia's last gas refinery, further constraining Russian energy infrastructure available to global markets
China's LNG import volumes rose for a second straight month, competing with Europe for available Atlantic Basin cargoes

power.summary: EU carbon allowances (EUA) jumped 4.2% to $78.44, tracking TTF's 40% monthly rally closely as gas-fired generation costs spike. A European heatwave is simultaneously elevating power demand while warming rivers and reducing hydro and nuclear cooling capacity, compounding the supply crunch. European diesel inventories are reportedly heading toward multi-year lows per Morgan Stanley analysis cited today. Ukraine's drone campaign struck Russian fuel hubs in Stavropol Krai and the power grid in occupied Crimea, keeping Russian energy infrastructure under pressure. Early-summer warnings of European jet fuel shortages proved premature according to one report, though diesel stress remains acute. US-Iran missile exchanges continued through day nine, with air raid sirens reported in Bahrain, signalling no near-term de-escalation.
drivers: TTF's 40% monthly surge flows directly into carbon pricing: EUA +4.2% today as gas generation cost curves shift higher
European heatwave stressing power grids via elevated demand and reduced river-based generation capacity
Ukraine drone strikes on Russian fuel hubs and Crimea power grid sustain structural risk premium on European energy supply
